retro:
# PR #12983 retrospective

## Effective

- Read-only security triage distinguished risky ordinary recovery commands from malicious instructions and avoided live reproduction.
- Both fresh technical sessions completed independent finals before any conclusions were read. The unchanged launcher supplied important context beyond the diff.
- Source adjudication bounded cleanup-race claims without needing a native desktop, tmpfs exhaustion or additional substitute fixtures.
- Audit review rejected broad synthetic success totals despite a valid seal and exit 0. Public claims use independent source evidence only.

## Deviations and remediation

Opus ran one host-side command-v dependency lookup instead of keeping it within review.py. No discovered backend was executed on the host. The later fixture lacked literal per-final-target assertions and producer guards across setup, quickshell/Hyprland stubs, summary/receipt appends and pipelines. These gaps violate assignment process requirements. Retained originals and audit-addendum.md document them. Validated totals, native timing generalizations and any actual tmpfs-full result claim were withdrawn. A successful run and a parent-root check cannot repair those missing guarantees.

The coordinator corrected the responsible prompt with a specific stub/callee audit reminder and an absolute-path requirement. Assignment originally gave the reviewer prompt path relatively; it resolved from state, but was unnecessarily ambiguous. Future assignments must provide its absolute path.

No evidence of host service, configuration, account, desktop or hardware mutation. Every synthetic runtime was inside review.py; namespace teardown ended its children. No source was changed for experiments. Private clones, raw logs and native session history were preserved. No quota exhaustion, fallback model or contaminated independent assessment occurred.

## What not to repeat

Do not build 22 substitute cases before validating a minimal case's full target/producer inventory. If a source predicate or synchronization gap establishes the bounded finding, stop there. Do not equate marker counts with guarded evidence. Do not claim real-process teardown timing from stub size. Keep lower-value supervisor behavior local until native user-visible impact is supported.

## Tool observations

No confirmed review.py or Omadev bug. No desktop slot was allocated. Herdr lifecycle and fresh editorial launch worked without trust-dialog intervention. All pages remain saved and unopened for the outer batch overview.
comment:
Two source-level correctness issues remain in the recovery path at `6fd5bf76`.

**Verified by source inspection:** the existing IPC stop loop is preserved, with TERM/KILL escalation added for matching processes that remain. Native recovery was not verified.

### Wait for termination before deciding which runtime directories are stale

[The SIGKILL loop and cleanup](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/6fd5bf76faee0945a4feb9e0a6512885195c1d5f/bin/omarchy-restart-shell#L89-L110) have no intervening completion check. Sending SIGKILL does not wait for termination or parent reaping; an exiting or unreaped process can still pass `kill -0`.

```text
SIGKILL sent
  -> PID still exists when cleanup checks it
  -> instance directory treated as live and skipped
  -> replacement launched without reclaiming that directory
```

**Impact:** If that directory contains the log filling runtime tmpfs, this recovery attempt can leave those bytes unreclaimed. This is timing-dependent; actual tmpfs-full recovery and native Quickshell registration were not tested.

**Suggested change:** Confirm the targeted process has exited and coordinate reaping as needed, then clean its stale runtime entry before launching the replacement. Use a bounded failure path if termination cannot be confirmed, rather than assuming signal delivery completes it.

### Match the config argument exactly before signalling

[The process filter](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/6fd5bf76faee0945a4feb9e0a6512885195c1d5f/bin/omarchy-restart-shell#L73-L94) flattens NUL-separated argv and searches for `$CONFIG_DIR` anywhere in the resulting string. It runs even after the IPC loop successfully stopped the intended shell.

Synthetic path example, directly implied by the predicate:

| Requested config | Other process's config | Current substring match |
|---|---|---|
| `/example/omarchy/shell` | `/example/omarchy/shell-dev` | Matches, so receives TERM/KILL escalation |

**Impact:** A routine restart can terminate a separate Quickshell configuration whose path merely contains the requested path. The same false match can occur in an unrelated argument.

**Suggested change:** Parse NUL-separated arguments and compare the actual config-path option precisely, accounting for supported option forms and path normalization, before selecting signal targets.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source inspection of both revisions, the launcher and tests. These findings rely on source control flow and Linux signal semantics, not a native desktop reproduction. The new recovery test checks syntax and source patterns, not these behaviors. Real Quickshell, locked-session recovery and tmpfs exhaustion remain untested.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** GPT 6 Astra Medium performed initial inspection and synthesis; Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh completed independent technical assessments. Claims were checked against the pinned source, followed by a fresh Astra Medium editorial check.
